translation_notes: the draft folded the two `self.grafoa.add((...))` calls on the shared subject into `self.grafoa += g{ }`, which the batch note flags as a known mechanical-draft bias for this stratum: `g{ }` builds a NEW, disposable graph, `+=` merges it into `self.grafoa` after the fact -- it happens to be isomorphism-preserving here but is not the construction the stratum measures. Rewrote as `@graph self.grafoa` (declared once, since `self.grafoa` is never reassigned in this function) followed by a single `+{ {subjektua} a {objektua} ; rdfs:label {Literal(...)} }`, which writes straight into the live graph.

`subjektua`/`objektua` are already-constructed `URIRef` values (from `self.bilatuUria`/`self.getType`, both computed above the fold), so they interpolate as bare `{expr}` in term position rather than through `f<...>` or `ex:{...}` -- there is no IRI literal or prefixed name to write, the terms are opaque Python values by the time the shared-subject fold sees them.

context shim (context_shim.py): `grafoaSortu` is a bare method extracted without its enclosing `TextToTriple` class (procesSource/source/gate_cloud.py @ 82875c5f94, JonAnderAsua/TFG-KG-RelacionesClientelares), so `self.grafoa`, `self.balioztatu`, `self.bilatuUria`, `self.getType` are all unbound. Fetched the real source from GitHub at this commit to write the shim faithfully: `getType` is copied VERBATIM (a pure function, safe to reproduce exactly). `balioztatu` in the real class blocks on `input()` to ask a human to confirm each classification, and `bilatuUria` issues a live SPARQL SELECT against `self.tripleStore` -- neither can run in this harness, so both are fixture-driven stand-ins keyed by annotation text, matching the CONTRACT `grafoaSortu` depends on (a bool+label pair, a URI string) without inventing their withheld interactive/networked logic. Identical shim imported by both original.py and translated.ldpy.

added a `demo(annotations, validations, uris)` harness (identical on both sides) that builds a fresh `TextToTripleStub`, calls `grafoaSortu`, and returns `self.grafoa`: the region mutates `self.grafoa` rather than returning it, and the stub has no `__eq__`, so comparing the `self` argument directly would compare object identity and always fail (same pattern as the Dewberry/blobfish region in this stratum).

fixture exercises the fold (two annotations sharing one subject text), all three `annotationType` values the `if` guard filters before `balioztatu` is even reached (Sentence/Money/Date), a `balioztatu` rejection (no triple), and the 'Location' special case in `getType` (-> schema:Place, not schema:Location).

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: the two lookups `i['annotationType']['value']` (2 uses) and `i['annotationText']['value']` (3 uses) become two local variables at the top of the try. Moving the text lookup ahead of the type test does not change the effect: a missing key raises inside the same bare `except: pass`, and nothing has been written yet in that iteration. The three `!=` joined by `and` become `not in ('Sentence', 'Money', 'Date')`, `if(balioztatu):` becomes `if balioztatu:`, `uria`/`objektua` are inlined, and the two `self.grafoa.add` calls become one `self.grafoa += [...]`. The call order (balioztatu, bilatuUria, getType) is unchanged.

Kept on both sides: the bare `try/except: pass` around each annotation, and the explicit `Literal(annotation_text)`: a bare `{annotation_text}` would raise on a JSON null where Literal(None) writes "None", and the bare except would then silently drop the triple.

optimized.ldpy, from optimized.py: `@graph self.grafoa` + one `+{ f<{self.bilatuUria(annotation_text)}> a f<{self.getType(obj)}> ; rdfs:label {Literal(annotation_text)} }`. `f<{x}>` is `URIRef(str(x))`, the same as URIRef(x) with no @base in scope. Exception to the symmetry rule: `subjektua` is inlined as the subject, because `;` writes it once. In Python it appears in both tuples, so it stays.
